A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same spectral reasoning study. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison despite substantial reorganization.

before.justification: V1 reports original MiniF2F and MATH classification experiments, robustness controls, architectural comparisons, and induction-head ablations, including appendix results.

after.justification: V2 retains original classification experiments and reports additional proof-search comparisons, supervised-probe comparisons, a manual proof audit, and runtime measurements.

M1.justification: The core graph construction, spectral diagnostics, threshold classifier, and Algorithm 1 remain unchanged. V2 adds HFER candidate reranking and a standardized log-probability/HFER ensemble in Section 4.6, and describes a k=50 Lanczos variant on A^T A in Appendix B.3. These extend the existing inference and computation procedures.

E1.justification: MiniF2F formal proofs and MATH informal reasoning remain the evaluated datasets. V2 adds proof-candidate selection through Best-of-16 search on MiniF2F, a limited task extension beyond validity classification. The informal-mathematics and mixture-of-experts evaluations already appeared in v1.

E2.justification: The comparison suite changes substantially. V2 adds proof-search comparisons with Token Entropy, Log-Prob, and a log-probability/HFER ensemble, plus Obeso et al. (2026) and local linear probes. V1's Attention Entropy, Gini Coefficient, and Max Concentration classification/authorship comparisons disappear. The MATH Logistic Regression and Random Guess rows are also removed, while Random Forest remains.

E3.justification: V2 introduces Best-of-16 sampling at temperature 0.7 with Pass@1 and AUC-ROC, probe comparisons with specified label budgets, and runtime comparisons at 1,000 and 10,000 tokens; 32,000-token timings are extrapolated. The reported balanced MATH subset changes from N=98 to N=106, without establishing a rerun. The original 60/20/20 split and nested 5-by-4-fold CV remain unchanged.

E4.justification: V2 removes the induction-head zeroing study from v1 Section 5.2 and its cross-model replications in Appendix G. It adds tactic-count difficulty stratification, layer-specific HFER/entropy separation analysis, and a reclaimed-proof failure audit. The basic authorship and human-perturbation controls and most Appendix C analyses are retained.

E5.justification: V2 adds 95% confidence intervals for the Layer 8 HFER and entropy effect sizes and reports two independent audit raters with Cohen's kappa=0.82. Existing CV uncertainty, difficulty-stratified accuracy intervals, significance tests, and multiple-comparison correction remain. No increase in repeated experimental runs is established.

E6.justification: Table 2's main classification results are unchanged. New results include HFER versus Log-Prob Pass@1 of 34.2% versus 29.8% on Llama-3.1-8B, probe AUC comparisons, tactic-stratified effect sizes, audit percentages, and a reported 61-fold runtime speedup at 10,000 tokens. These are additional experiments, not improvements on rerun v1 settings. Detailed two-feature results, attention-baseline comparisons, and induction-ablation findings are removed.

T1.justification: Section 3's mathematical definitions and Appendix A's Laplacian properties, proof, Fiedler and Cheeger statements, and graph Fourier definitions are unchanged apart from numbering and typesetting. V2 adds no substantive theorem, proof, or derivation.

C1.justification: V2 expands the headline contributions to difficulty-wide robustness, demonstrated Best-of-16 gains of 4.4–6.6 percentage points, a claimed 98% of supervised AUC with zero labels, and real-time operation at 32,000 tokens. V1 presented proof-search integration as a prospective application. The central cross-architecture spectral-validity claim remains.

C2.justification: V1 asserts an induction-head causal mechanism; v2 removes that analysis and calls the method a correlation-based diagnostic in Section 8, although its abstract still claims causal confirmation. V2 also acknowledges the weaker informal-reasoning signal, excludes unstructured-text generalization, qualifies long-context deployment, and adds a confident-hallucination explanation for reranking. Architectural and cognitive interpretations largely survive in Appendix D.

D1.justification: V2 documents the Lanczos k=50 computation, proof-generation temperature, probe layer, and label budgets, and states that the code includes Lanczos acceleration. It removes the separate spectral-trust library/PyPI disclosure and detailed per-model two-feature rules. Hardware specifications and the promised evaluation-subset release remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The introduction and related work substantially shift toward neural manifold geometry and internal-state hallucination detection, adding work by Canatar, Chou, Draye, Healy, Bhatnagar, and others. Obeso et al. becomes an explicit comparator. Earlier coverage of sparse autoencoders, test-time scaling, and the author's two spectral studies is removed or reduced.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, related work, and discussion are extensively rewritten and compressed. Architectural, mixture-of-experts, and cognitive discussions move into Appendix D; several experimental and causal sections disappear. Dedicated Limitations, Impact Statement, and Ethical Considerations sections are added, substantially changing the narrative structure.

P2.justification: V2 adopts a two-column conference layout for the main text, adds an overview diagram, introduces highlighted tables, and resizes or relocates retained plots. New comparison and audit tables replace several earlier displays. V1's causal Figure 4 and appendix Figures 14–19 are removed, while the layer-wise spectral plots remain.

improvement.justification: V2 adds useful downstream comparisons, failure auditing, and more appropriate scope limitations, but removes detailed baseline and causal evidence. New headline claims also conflict with the supporting material: Table 5's approximately 98% supervised-AUC ratio requires 50 calibration labels, whereas zero-shot AUC is 0.923 versus 0.981; the abstract still claims causal confirmation despite removal of the ablations and Section 8's diagnostic-only qualification. These evidential gains and reporting losses prevent a reliable net-quality judgment.
